identity.description: Count regression for OVERDISPERSED data: a Poisson mean with a gamma-mixed rate, adding an estimated dispersion parameter alpha so variance = mean + alpha*mean^2 (NB2). The honest upgrade from Poisson when variance outruns the mean — same log-linear coefficients, correctly-sized standard errors.

consumes.note: target must be a non-negative integer count

emits.note: predicted mean count; the fitted NB family plus estimated alpha defines a full predictive count distribution
log rate ratios with SEs plus the estimated dispersion alpha (reported with its own SE)

loglike_method.note: nb2: variance = mu + alpha*mu^2 (standard); nb1: variance = mu + alpha*mu; geometric: alpha fixed at 1

alpha.note: fit_regularized L1 penalty strength (NOT the dispersion parameter, which is estimated by MLE); 0.0 = plain fit

maxiter.note: statsmodels discrete-model default; raise on non-convergence

invariances.why: unpenalized MLE is scale-equivariant, but the searchable L1 penalty (fit_regularized) is unit-dependent, and poorly-scaled columns condition the BFGS Hessian badly enough to stall convergence
log-linear mean structure: a monotone transform of a covariate changes the fitted mean function
the likelihood has no missing-value mechanism; rows must be imputed or are dropped

assumes the conditional distribution is Negative Binomial (gamma-mixed Poisson): variance = mean + alpha*mean^2 under NB2 — overdispersion is modeled explicitly, but a variance that grows on a different power law is still misspecified
the extra dispersion parameter is weakly identified at very small n — alpha's MLE needs a few hundred rows to stabilize; coefficient estimates remain usable earlier with wide CIs
log-linear form extends the mean beyond the observed covariate range, with the same exponential-growth caution as Poisson

featureStats.why: variance/mean of the target is the reason to be at this node at all — a ratio near 1 means Poisson suffices (alpha would sit at its zero boundary); well above 1 is NB's home turf

NB's fatter tail absorbs more zeros than Poisson for the same mean, but an observed zero share still exceeding the NB-implied one indicates a second structural-zero mechanism — the commit-zero-inflated signal
the NB likelihood is defined only on non-negative integers; anything else is a reject-input, not a modeling choice

modelMetrics.why: the boundary likelihood-ratio test of alpha=0 vs Poisson — if alpha is not significantly above zero, the extra parameter buys nothing and the honest commit is back to Poisson
residual dispersion AFTER modeling overdispersion — still >> 1 means the NB2 variance law itself is wrong (try nb1, or the mechanism is zero-inflation)

edgeCases.behavior: dispersion estimate pins to the boundary; its SE and Wald test are invalid there

edgeCases.note: raise maxiter, use Poisson fit as start_params

edgeCases.behavior: alpha inflates to absorb the zero mass, distorting the variance law

driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: add_constant; predict returns the mean count; surface the fitted dispersion alpha alongside coefficients

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; incomplete rows are dropped, biasing both mean and dispersion estimates
log/Yeo-Johnson of skewed covariates improves the log-linear mean fit
MLE is scale-equivariant unpenalized, but standardization conditions BFGS and is needed whenever the L1 penalty is active
categoricals must be design-encoded before fitting
